liam: Quick q — trying to capture nsys traces that clearly show kernel selection + KV-cache handoffs. My short captures keep missing tiny kernels (the ones that pick quantized vs fp path). Any recommended CLI flags/flow for reliable, compact runs?

sara: Use --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt so you get device kernels, our NVTX markers, and the OSRT sampling stream. Also enable CPU sampling so host-side work (threads doing batching / eviction) shows up. For tiny kernels bracket the region with NVTX and avoid one-shot <1s captures.

jonas: +1 on bracketed captures. Do a warmup outside the capture window then `--capture-range=nvtx` (push/pop around the interesting section). If you capture mid-warmup you'll bias OSRT sampling. Try 5–20s captures depending on sequence length.

aj: For KV handoff specifically, you need enough time to see an eviction or refill. I typically run `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --output=foo.qdrep --capture-range=nvtx --duration=12s python -m canary.run` and wrap NVTX around forward + KV update points. Use --force-overwrite if iterating.

perf-bot: Heads up — large, unfiltered qdrep files > ~2GB are painful in the GUI. Use `nsys export` to slice windows or export CSV aggregates for quick checks. Also consider `--compress` if your CLI supports it to save disk.

liam: Helpful, thanks. Any tips to make kernel-selection differences (int8 vs fp32) obvious in the timeline?

sara: Put NVTX metadata with model/version/quantization mode and batch_size. On the timeline filter by `Device Activity` and inspect kernel names — many kernels include dtype/variant suffixes. Use zoom + grouping by kernel name to spot which variant is launched per NVTX span.

jonas: Also run back-to-back captures with only quantization toggled; diff the `nsys stats --report=kernel` outputs. Kernel duration/SM utilization will differ and show up in aggregates even if tiny on timeline.

aj: One more nuance: OSRT sampling can miss very short-lived kernels if your sample window is too coarse. Do bracketed + repeated runs with small offsets (0ms, 20ms, 50ms) to de-bias sampling. If you suspect missed kernels, increase capture duration slightly rather than cranking sampling frequency.

ops-bot: Reminder: run these on canary GPUs (canary-gpu43) to minimize noise. Attach NVTX tags with git sha, model name, seq_len, batch_size so we can correlate traces to code.

liam: OK i'll run a set of 12s bracketed captures with NVTX tags and post the qdrep + `nsys stats` output. If i paste the command / flags here will someone sanity-check before i spam S3?

sara: :thumbsup: ping me + jonas when you post, we'll scan for missing flags (duration, trace, capture-range, cpu sampling) and sampling bias issues.
_meta: This thread is a short eng-runtime Slack conversation about nsys CLI flags, bracketed capture strategy, OSRT sampling bias, and practical tips for capturing kernel selection and KV cache handoffs. Messages are intentionally terse and include example commands and small operational notes.
